This neuron is a diffuse syntactic-boundary detector: it peaks on function words and punctuation that close or hinge a clause mid-sentence — the "order" of "in order to", complementizer "that", auxiliary "had", and the quote-closing `',` / `."` / `!"` sequences in quoted speech or code argument lists — rather than on any semantic content (it is suppressed on similar clause-initial tokens like "a", "have", "providing" and on sentence-final periods after names).

L10·N5755unmasked layer

L13·N270unmasked layer
Fires on the token that begins a re-statement/continuation of wording already used nearby — typically the first word of a new sentence or clause right after a period/parenthetical (e.g. "Ugh", "Cures", "This cookie", "the client executable", the second "and" in a repeated "cute and cuddly"); the same function words ("and", "are", "at", hyphen) get strongly negative activation in non-repetitive list/boilerplate contexts, so it is a clause-onset/repetition-resumption detector rather than a lexical one.
